newsitem.title: USA: Record Iran wheat imports tied to poor crop--USDA.
newsitem.headline: Record Iran wheat imports tied to poor crop--USDA.

text.p: The best explanation for Iran's surprising position as the world's largest wheat importer may be a rain-spoiled 1996 harvest, a high-level U.S. Agriculture Department analyst said Friday.

"There's all sorts of speculation," said Gerald Rector, chairman of the department's world wheat estimating committee. "The major one we've been hearing is they had a lot of rain at the time they would have been harvesting last year."
A poor quality crop would mean less wheat for making bread and could spur Iran to look to outside suppliers.
In an April 14 report, USDA said Iran would be the largest wheat importing nation in 1996/97, buying 6.5 million tonnes, roughly double its usual purchases.
The International Grains Council, based in London, agreed Thursday in its monthly appraisal of grain trade. It pegged Iranian imports at 6.6 million tonnes in the year ending June 30.
Because of poor diplomatic relations between Iran and the United States, "nobody really knows why they're buying so much," Rector said.

While some analysts have speculated some of the imports might go to Afghanistan or Iraq, others contend the Moslem-populated former Soviet republics were more likely customers if wheat was being re-exported.
"In Iran, things travel to other places as well," said one grain trade source in Washington, who noted smuggling was common in Central Asia.
Another grain trade source said Iran's record imports probably were related to the size of its domestic crop.
USDA has forecast ever-larger imports by Iran for the past few months.

"In Iran, a low government procurement price and heavy on-farm feeding of the second poor-quality wheat crop in as many years has resulted in an import level which is forecast to reach 6.5 million (metric) tons, up another one-half million tons from last month's increase and more than twice the prior year's amount," USDA said in its April 14 "Grain: World Markets and Trade" report.
"As increasingly anticipated, Iran is now expected to become the world's top importer of wheat for the 1996/97 season."
Iranian imports were pegged at six million tonnes by USDA in March and at five million tonnes in February.
